review_notes: I read the whole file as supplied and used greps to confirm line numbers and that `oldPointwiseModule` and `pointwiseModule_eq_old` are used only inside this file. Nothing was compiled, so every rewrite below is untested. Candidate 0 is the clearest case. Candidate 1 is a real duplicated construction, but I could not rule out a module-system reason for the inlining. Candidate 2 shares only a short preamble. claims.reason: `ring_map_ι` (line 225) and `group_map_ι` (line 236) have the same proof: `change (ι ≫ (pointwiseLeftKanExtension _).map g).hom _ = _`, then `erw [Functor.pointwiseLeftKanExtension_map, colimit.ι_desc]`, then `rfl`. They differ only in which presheaf is used: `R` in `RingCat` or `M.presheaf` in `AddCommGrpCat`. The categorical content is that the generator map ι_i followed by the Kan-extension map along g is ι at (CostructuredArrow.map g).obj i. That statement does not use ring or group structure. Both `RingCat.{v}` and `AddCommGrpCat.{v}` are `Type (v+1)` categories with `HasColimits`. The file already states `pointwiseToPullback` for a general `C : Type (v+1)` with `[HasColimits C]`, so the generic form fits the file's conventions. The proof is short, so this is borderline. The delicate `erw` part is repeated verbatim, though, and a generic lemma would also serve `pointwiseMap_ι`, which uses the sibling `colimit.ι_map` step. I have not compiled the refactor. The corollaries may need `erw` or `by exact` to match the `.hom` coercion.
claims.shared_lemma:
private theorem ι_pointwiseLeftKanExtension_map (C : Type (v+1)) [Category.{v} C] [HasColimits C] (F : Y.Presheaf C) {U V : Opens X} (g : op U ⟶ op V) (i : index f U) :
  colimit.ι (CostructuredArrow.proj (Opens.map f).op (op U) ⋙ F) i ≫ ((Opens.map f).op.pointwiseLeftKanExtension F).map g =
  colimit.ι (CostructuredArrow.proj (Opens.map f).op (op V) ⋙ F) ((CostructuredArrow.map g).obj i) := by
  erw [Functor.pointwiseLeftKanExtension_map, colimit.ι_desc]; rfl
rewritten_uses: theorem ring_map_ι ... := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (ι_pointwiseLeftKanExtension_map f RingCat.{v} R g i) r
theorem group_map_ι ... := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (ι_pointwiseLeftKanExtension_map f AddCommGrpCat.{v} M.presheaf g i) m

claims.reason: `pointwiseModule` (line 145) rebuilds `oldPointwiseModule` (line 130) in full. Both transport the native `ModuleColimit` module structure along `groupIso`, using `AddEquiv.module`, and then restrict scalars along `ringIso.symm` with `Module.compHom`. `pointwiseModule` re-inlines the `IsFiltered` instance, the `InitiallySmall` instance, `indexProj`, `indexedRing`, `indexedModule`, `ringIso` and `groupIso`. `pointwiseModule_eq_old` (line 188) proves the two are `rfl`-equal, and the greps show `oldPointwiseModule` and that theorem are used only in that bridge. So one transport construction is maintained twice. The likely reason for the inlining is that a public, exposed instance should not mention private helpers. I could not verify that, and I found no Lean error message for the case. If it is the reason, the fix is to make the helpers (`meetIndex`, `meetLeft`, `meetRight`, `ringIso`, `groupIso`, and the `IsFiltered` and `InitiallySmall` instances) non-private. That is a small visibility change, not a cycle. I have not compiled this.

claims.reason: The shared part of `restriction_smul` and `pointwiseMap_smul` is only a three-line preamble. It does `obtain ⟨i,a,b,ha,hb⟩ := pointwise_jointly_surjective …`, then `erw [← ha, ← hb]`, then `erw [← pointwise_smul_ι …]`. The real arguments after that are different: `group_map_ι`/`ring_map_ι` followed by `pointwise_smul_ι` at V, versus `pointwiseMap_ι` followed by `map_smul` and `pointwise_smul_ι` at N. The proposed lemma would only move this preamble into a helper. It would be a thin wrapper over `pointwise_jointly_surjective` and `pointwise_smul_ι`, which already hold the real content. The two proofs also work in different settings: one has a single module M and two opens, the other has two modules M and N over the same open. A single helper statement would have to be stated over `pointwiseSmul`, and the proofs would then have to be re-adapted from their `letI` instance selection to it. The saving is small and the risk to the instance-sensitive `erw` steps is real. This is not a nontrivial repeated argument.

evidence.excerpt:
obtain ⟨i, a, b, ha, hb⟩ := pointwise_jointly_surjective f R M U r m
  erw [← ha, ← hb]
  erw [← pointwise_smul_ι f R M U i a b]
  erw [group_map_ι f R M g i (a • b), ring_map_ι f R g i a,
    group_map_ι f R M g i b]
  exact pointwise_smul_ι f R M V ((CostructuredArrow.map g).obj i) a b

erw [pointwiseMap_ι f φ U i (a • b), pointwiseMap_ι f φ U i b]
  rw [map_smul, pointwise_smul_ι f R N U i]
  rfl
